constraint_decided_it: Nothing in domain/range or FOL separated them -- both apply P14 (E7 -> E39, many to many necessary 1,n:0,n) to E11 Modification with P14.1 roles, and both correctly keep the museum officer off P14 under the 'active participation / implies causal or legal responsibility' clause. What separated them is source fidelity: P14's only worked example is a single actor, 'The painting of the Sistine Chapel (E7) carried out by Michelangelo Buonaroti (E21) in the role of master craftsman (E55)', and B attributes to that dossier a supervisor-plus-'implied hands-on assistants' pairing the source does not contain, while A's quotations (P14's example, t1546 'patients in a surgery are necessary, but do not carry it out', t1477 'Scriptorium of, Workshop of, Circle of, Studio of') all verify verbatim.
better_modelling: E11 Modification (scope note: 'It also includes the conservation treatment of an object'), P31 has modified (E11 -> E18) the six cabinets; P14 -> studio principal with P14.1 'supervisor/master craftsman' and P14 -> each apprentice with P14.1 'executant', since P14 is many to many and the apprentices' hands-on work plus the principal's supervisory responsibility both satisfy 'active participation ... implies causal or legal responsibility'; optionally P14 -> the workshop as E74 Group for the invoice-level legal responsibility. The museum officer is excluded from P14 by t1546, where Doerr rules that necessary presence is not 'causal', Velios proposes 'active without sharing the responsibility of the activity ... P11 had participant should be used instead', and Sanderson concurs; so P11 had participant (E5 -> E39) is the SIG-named fallback, with her visits better recorded as their own E14 Condition Assessment ('assessing the state of preservation of an object during a particular period ... may be carried out by inspection'). A supplies everything except P31 and the E14 specialisation; B supplies P31 and E14 but misses the t1546 line that actually decides the officer.
reasoning: Both answers land on the same prescribed modelling and neither violates a domain, range or FOL clause: P14's domain E7 covers E11 Modification, its range E39 covers all three persons, and its (1,n:0,n) quantification plus P14.1 licenses recording principal and apprentices together with distinguishing roles. A is verdict correct -- every attributed string checks out, and its exclusion of the conservation officer rests on the one thread that actually settles the question (t1546, where Doerr's surgery-patient case and Velios's proposed redirect to P11 draw exactly this line); its only defect is under-specifying her visits as generic 'monitoring/inspection acts' where E14 Condition Assessment exists. B reaches the same conclusion and is modelling-wise marginally richer (P31 has modified, E14 for the visits), but its load-bearing justification -- that the P14 dossier's Michelangelo example 'pairs a supervising master craftsman role with implied hands-on assistants' -- is not in the source, and its E14 quotation 'may be carried out by inspection... during a particular period' splices two fragments in reverse order; B also asserts in its notes that no SIG precedent was found, when t1546 is squarely on point. Per the strict rule that a source not saying what an answer claims is unsupported even when the conclusion is right, B takes the harsher verdict; the margin is slight because the prescribed modelling itself is the same.
